summary: E2E backend test of Supabase migration: 32/37 passed (86%). Auth (all 3 roles + /me + /google/url), Batches (public list, by-code, admin CRUD, predefined protection), Classes + Tests + batch-isolation on JEEM2027 side, Live-Class Zoom create/start/join + raise-hand flow, Announcements (create + JEEM student sees + delete), Notifications (unread + mark read), Questions with option-images (Part 6), and question-samples all work. Frontend loads: /landing, /login, /signup, /admission, /auth/callback all render with proper titles; student login succeeds and lands on /dashboard; /profile shows roll_number (NXU-...). Three real backend bugs found — admission signup, image upload bucket, and Zoom S2S scopes. Because admission is broken, the NEX2028 isolation test and the NEX2028 negative-announcement test could not fully complete (but the JEEM positive side is confirmed).

critical.issue: Returns 400 'Signup failed: User not allowed' (Supabase 403 on POST /auth/v1/admin/users). Root cause: get_supabase() returns a singleton client. The successful call to supabase.auth.sign_in_with_password() inside /api/auth/login mutates the shared client's Authorization header to the user's JWT. All subsequent supabase.auth.admin.* calls (create_user in admission_routes and auth_routes signup) then send the user's JWT instead of the SERVICE_ROLE key, so Supabase Auth Admin API returns 403. Startup seed works because it runs before any login. FIX OPTIONS: (a) use a dedicated service-role client for admin ops (e.g. get_admin_supabase()), (b) after every sign_in_with_password call sign_out() to reset headers, or (c) call POST /auth/v1/admin/users directly with httpx using SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. Option (a) is cleanest.

500 'Bucket not found'. The bucket 'question-images' does not exist in Supabase Storage, and _ensure_bucket() cannot auto-create it because supabase-py's create_bucket signature is different — logs show: 'ensure_bucket failed: {statusCode:400, error:Error, message:body/name must be string}'. Fix: use supabase.storage.create_bucket(id=BUCKET, options={'public': True}) with keyword args, or create the bucket manually in Supabase dashboard (recommended).

minor.issue: The Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app is missing scopes. Logs: 'Invalid access token, does not contain scopes:[user:read:token, user:read:token:admin]' when fetching host ZAK (start_url would still work), 'dashboard:read:list_meeting_participants:admin' → participants list is always empty for teacher, and 'meeting:delete:meeting:admin, meeting:delete:meeting' → delete-meeting call silently fails (caught). Meeting create + SDK signature generation both work fine. Fix requires adding those scopes in the Zoom App Marketplace (not code).
Will hit the same 'User not allowed' bug as admissions once any login has been performed — same root cause (shared supabase client).

integration_issues.issue: Sidebar still contains links to PYQ Section, Analytics, Bookmarks — these routes are deferred/removed per this migration scope and will 404 when clicked. Either hide the sidebar items or reintroduce the pages later.

action_items: FIX (critical): Split get_supabase() into two clients — one anon+session for user auth, one service-role-only for admin.* operations. Root fix for admission-signup 403 and future /api/auth/signup regressions.

FIX (critical): Manually create Supabase Storage bucket 'question-images' (public) in the Supabase Dashboard, OR fix _ensure_bucket() to use the correct supabase-py 2.x signature: supabase.storage.create_bucket(BUCKET, options={'public': True}).

FIX (config): Add scopes to Zoom S2S OAuth app: user:read:token, dashboard:read:list_meeting_participants:admin, meeting:delete:meeting:admin. Without these the teacher /participants endpoint returns an empty Zoom list (raise-hand DB list still works) and delete-meeting silently fails.
Consider hiding deferred sidebar items (PYQ, Analytics, Bookmarks) from Dashboard until routes are re-implemented.

After admission fix, re-run test_admission_creates_user_and_roll, test_admission_me, test_nex2028_student_isolation and test_nex_student_does_not_see (announcements) to complete full isolation coverage.
critical_code_review_comments: config/database.py get_supabase() returns a single lazily-constructed Client. supabase-py mutates this client's default auth headers on sign_in_with_password, breaking admin.* calls. This is the direct cause of the admission 403.

routes/admission_routes.py wraps the Supabase error as a generic 'Signup failed: <msg>' — that swallows the fact that it's actually a permission problem. Consider surfacing 500 for anything other than the 'already registered' branch so the RCA is obvious in prod.

routes/upload_routes.py _ensure_bucket() catches all exceptions with just a warning — a missing bucket then causes every upload to fail with a confusing 500. Prefer failing loudly at startup or fixing the create call.
services/seed_service.py updates every seed user's password on every startup — noisy but idempotent; consider gating behind an env flag for prod.

notification_routes.py list_notifications returns {notifications, unread_count} at top-level (no 'success') while every other endpoint uses {'success': True, ...} — small consistency drift for the frontend.

student_test_routes.py submit() computes correct/incorrect purely from client-supplied 'is_correct' — a student can trivially post is_correct:true for every answer to inflate their score. Server should verify against the tests.questions correct_answers list.

rca of the issue: 1) ADMISSION 403: supabase-py Client is a singleton; sign_in_with_password mutates its auth header to the newly-signed-in user's JWT; subsequent auth.admin.create_user is sent with that user JWT (no admin scope) → 403. Reproducible by (a) restart backend (b) hit /api/auth/login (any user) (c) hit /api/admissions/submit → always 403 thereafter. 2) UPLOAD 500: bucket 'question-images' never existed in Supabase Storage; _ensure_bucket's auto-create call passes the bucket name positionally to a supabase-py signature that now expects it as a keyword+options-dict, so bucket creation silently no-ops and every upload 404s. 3) ZOOM SCOPES: Zoom S2S app was built with only meeting:write/read scopes; participants/dashboard and delete endpoints require additional admin scopes not granted.
